56331-the-historical-growth-of-the-engli.description: A book by A. Hamilton Thompson. The early history of the English parish church is obscure, owing to the fact that architectural remains of the earliest fabrics are somewhat scanty, and that their actual date still affords ground for dispute.

arxiv-1802-07657.title: DNA-Graphene Interactions During Translocation Through Nanogaps
arxiv-1802-07657.creator: Hiral N. Patel
arxiv-1802-07657.description: Abstract Abstract We study how double-stranded DNA translocates through graphene nanogaps. Nanogaps are fabricated with a novel capillary-force induced graphene nanogap formation technique. DNA translocation signatures for nanogaps are qualitatively different from those obtained with circular nanopores, owing to the distinct shape of the gaps discussed here.

arxiv-2011-12175.creator: X. H. Zheng 1, J. X. Zheng 2
arxiv-2011-12175.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by X. H. Zheng 1, J. X. Zheng 2. The Wheeler equation, for electromagnetic disturbances in a gravitational field, was found by Fiziev to have exact solutions both above and below the event horizon, in the form of waves propagating both inwardly and outwardly.

arxiv-2104-09077.title: Global Well-posedness of Incompressible Elastodynamics in Three Dimensional Thin Domain
arxiv-2104-09077.creator: Yuan Cai, Fan Wang
arxiv-2104-09077.description: Abstract In this article, we prove global existence of classical solutions to the incompressible isotropic Hookean elastodynamics in three-dimensional thin domain Ω δ = ℝ 2 × [ 0 , δ ] \Omega_{\delta}=\mathbb{R}^{2}\times[0,\delta] with periodic boundary condition. This system is essentially two dimensional quasilinear wave type equations.

arxiv-2106-08667.title: Photoionized Herbig-Haro objects in the Orion Nebula through deep high-spectral resolution spectroscopy II: HH 204 Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2106-08667.creator: J. E. Méndez-Delgado, W. J. Henney, C. Esteban, J. García-Rojas, A. Mesa-Delgado, K. Z. Arellano-Córdova
arxiv-2106-08667.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. E. Méndez-Delgado, W. J. Henney, C. Esteban, J. García-Rojas, A. Mesa-Delgado, K. Z. Arellano-Córdova. We analyze the physical conditions, chemical composition and other properties of the photoionized Herbig-Haro object HH 204 through Very Large Telescope (VLT) echelle spectroscopy and Hubble Space Telescope ( HST ) imaging. We kinematically isolate the high-velocity emission of HH 204 from the emission of the background nebula and study the sub-arcsecond distribution of physical conditions and ionic abundances across the HH object.

arxiv-2108-10516.creator: Robert Warnock
arxiv-2108-10516.description: Abstract This paper continues the work of two previous treatments of bunch lengthening by a passive harmonic cavity in an electron storage ring. Such cavities, intended to reduce the effect of Touschek scattering, are a feature of fourth generation synchrotron light sources.

arxiv-2110-07955.title: Macroscopic elastic stress and strain produced by irradiation
arxiv-2110-07955.creator: Luca Reali, Max Boleininger, Mark R. Gilbert, Sergei L. Dudarev
arxiv-2110-07955.description: Abstract Using the notion of eigenstrain produced by the defects formed in a material exposed to high energy neutron irradiation, we develop a method for computing macroscopic elastic stress and strain arising in components of a fusion power plant during operation.

arxiv-2207-07974.title: Online Prediction in Sub-linear Space Part of work done while interning at Google.
arxiv-2207-07974.creator: Binghui Peng, Fred Zhang
arxiv-2207-07974.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Binghui Peng, Fred Zhang. We provide the first sub-linear space and sub-linear regret algorithm for online learning with expert advice (against an oblivious adversary), addressing an open question raised recently by Srinivas, Woodruff, Xu and Zhou (STOC 2022). We also demonstrate a separation between oblivious and (strong) adaptive adversaries by proving a linear memory lower bound of any sub-linear regret algorithm against an adaptive adversary.

arxiv-2209-06438.title: Time rescaling of a primal-dual dynamical system with asymptotically vanishing damping
arxiv-2209-06438.creator: David Alexander Hulett, Dang-Khoa Nguyen
arxiv-2209-06438.description: Abstract In this work, we approach the minimization of a continuously differentiable convex function under linear equality constraints by a second-order dynamical system with an asymptotically vanishing damping term. The system under consideration is a time rescaled version of another system previously found in the literature.

arxiv-2212-09031.creator: Tao Yang, Zhichao Xu, Zhenduo Wang, Anh Tran, Qingyao Ai
arxiv-2212-09031.description: Abstract . Ranking systems are ubiquitous in modern Internet services, including online marketplaces, social media, and search engines. Traditionally, ranking systems only focus on how to get better relevance estimation. When relevance estimation is available, they usually adopt a user-centric optimization strategy where ranked lists are generated by sorting items according to their estimated relevance.

arxiv-2305-05733.title: Algorithms as Social-Ecological-Technological Systems: an Environmental Justice Lens on Algorithmic Audits Conference: 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency; June 12–15, 2023; USA 2023 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT ’23), June 12–15, 2
arxiv-2305-05733.creator: Bogdana Rakova, Roel Dobbe
arxiv-2305-05733.description: Abstract . This paper reframes algorithmic systems as intimately connected to and part of social and ecological systems, and proposes a first-of-its-kind methodology for environmental justice-oriented algorithmic audits. How do we consider environmental and climate justice dimensions of the way algorithmic systems are designed, developed, and deployed?

arxiv-2312-17213.title: Possible Unconventional Surface Superconductivity in the Half-Heusler YPtBi
arxiv-2312-17213.creator: Eylon Persky, Alan Fang, Xinyang Zhang, Carolina Adamo, Phillip Wu, Eli Levenson-Falk, Chandra Shekhar, Claudia Felser, Binghai Yan, Aharon Kapitulnik
arxiv-2312-17213.description: Abstract We report an extensive study of the noncentrosymmetric half-Heusler superconductor YPtBi, revealing an unusual relation between bulk superconductivity and the possible appearance of surface superconductivity on the (111) oriented surface, at temperatures up to 3 times the bulk transition temperature.

arxiv-2402-15439.description: Abstract . While ethical challenges are widely discussed in HCI, far less is reported about the ethical processes that researchers routinely navigate. We reflect on a multispecies project that negotiated an especially complex ethical approval process. Cat Royale was an artist-led exploration of creating an artwork to engage audiences in exploring trust in autonomous systems.

arxiv-2412-07893.title: BBN-simple : How to Bake a Universe-Sized Cake
arxiv-2412-07893.creator: Aidan Meador-Woodruff, Dragan Huterer
arxiv-2412-07893.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Aidan Meador-Woodruff, Dragan Huterer. Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN), the process of creation of lightest elements in the early universe, is a highly robust, precise, and ultimately successful theory that forms one of the three pillars of the standard hot-Big-Bang cosmological model. Existing theoretical treatments of BBN and the associated computer codes are accurate and flexible, but are typically highly technical and opaque, and not suitable for pedagogical understanding of the BBN.

arxiv-2505-10575.creator: Adnan Ahmad, Bahareh Nakisa, Mohammad Naim Rastgoo
arxiv-2505-10575.description: Abstract Emotion recognition through physiological signals such as electroencephalogram (EEG) has become an essential aspect of affective computing and provides an objective way to capture human emotions. However, physiological data characterized by cross-subject variability and noisy labels hinder the performance of emotion recognition models.

arxiv-2506-11805.creator: Li-Juan Cheng, Rui-Yu Yang
arxiv-2506-11805.description: Abstract In this paper, we establish a new global Hessian matrix estimate for heat-type equations on Riemannian manifolds using a Bismut-type Hessian formula. Our results feature fully explicit coefficients as well as delay / growth rate functions. These estimates yield two key applications: a novel backward weak Harnack inequality and a precise pointwise Hessian estimate for eigenfunctions.

arxiv-2510-02318.creator: Michael C. Donohue, Kedir Hussen, Oliver Langford, Richard Gallardo, Gustavo Jimenez-Maggiora, Paul S. Aisen, for the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
arxiv-2510-02318.description: Abstract Sharing clinical research data is essential for advancing research in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and other therapeutic areas. However, challenges in data accessibility, standardization, documentation, usability, and reproducibility continue to impede this goal. In this article, we highlight the advantages of using R packages to overcome these challenges using two examples.

pmc-10528786.title: Spectroscopic investigation of a Co(0001) model catalyst during exposure to H2 and CO at near-ambient pressures†

pmc-10528786.description: Cobalt catalysts, although already used industrially for Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, are prone to a number of deactivation mechanisms such as oxidation of the active phase, and the deposition of carbon and reaction products. We have performed near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy on Co(0001) model catalysts during exposure to gases relevant to Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, i.e., CO and H2, at 0.25 mbar total pressure.

pmc-10692100.title: Genetic diversity modulates the physical and transcriptomic response of skeletal muscle to simulated microgravity in male mice
pmc-10692100.creator: Yasmina Zeineddine, Michael A Friedman, Evan G Buettmann, Lovell B Abraham, Gabriel A Hoppock, Henry J Donahue
pmc-10692100.description: Developments in long-term space exploration necessitate advancements in countermeasures against microgravity-induced skeletal muscle loss. Astronaut data shows considerable variation in muscle loss in response to microgravity. Previous experiments suggest that genetic background influences the skeletal muscle response to unloading, but no in-depth analysis of genetic expression has been performed.

pmc-11450743.title: Practical Approach to Longitudinal Neurologic Care of Adults With X-Linked Adrenoleukodystrophy and Adrenomyeloneuropathy
pmc-11450743.creator: Alexandra B. Kornbluh, Aaron Baldwin, Ali Fatemi, Adeline Vanderver, Laura A. Adang, Keith Van Haren, Jacinda Sampson, Florian S. Eichler, Reza Sadjadi, Marc Engelen, Jennifer L. Orthmann-Murphy
pmc-11450743.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Although X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) has historically been considered a childhood disease managed by pediatric neurologists, it is one of the most common leukodystrophies diagnosed in adulthood. An increase in both male and female adults reaching diagnosis due to familial cases identified by state newborn screening panels and more widespread use of genetic testing results in a large cohort of presymptomatic or early symptomatic adults. This population is in urgent need of standardized assessments and follow-up care.

pmc-11458372.title: The sympathetic nervous system shapes the tumor microenvironment to impair chemotherapy response
pmc-11458372.creator: Annabel V. Manoleras, Erica K. Sloan, Aeson Chang
pmc-11458372.description: The tumor microenvironment influences cancer progression and response to treatments, which ultimately impacts the survival of patients with cancer. The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is a core component of solid tumors that arise in the body. In addition to influencing cancer progression, a role for the SNS in the effectiveness of cancer treatments is beginning to emerge.

pmc-11663013.description: Satellite DNAs (satDNAs) are tandemly repeated sequences that make up a significant portion of almost all eukaryotic genomes. In prior work, we considered biophysically relevant neuronal models to account for the observed magnitude of membrane voltage fluctuations.

While deep brain stimulation (DBS) shows therapeutic promise, the long-term persistence of its effects remains understudied. Expression patterns of circulating miRNAs, proposed diagnostic biomarkers, and their modulation by DBS are still poorly characterized in longitudinal studies.

pmc-12649461.creator: Junjie Qiu, Jiaxin Shi, Zhansheng Chen, Paul E Rapp
pmc-12649461.description: From the targets’ perspective, objectification is the process of being perceived and treated as mere instruments without human qualities. We argue that objectified people would experience more social pain and that the state of gratitude could weaken the link between objectification and painful feelings. Three studies (N = 927) confirmed our hypotheses.

pmc-13085732.title: Women’s experiences and perceptions of postpartum care in Saudi Arabia: a qualitative study
pmc-13085732.creator: Fatimah Almalki, Noura Alomair
pmc-13085732.description: BackgroundPostpartum care is essential for maternal well-being, yet limited qualitative work in Saudi Arabia has explored how women make sense of early postnatal experiences. This study explored postpartum women’s experiences of birth and hospital care and how perceived emotional, informational, and cultural support shaped recovery and health-promoting behaviours.
